page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.2xlarge is a storage-focused virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. A defining characteristic of this instance is its bundled local storage, which consists of 23,622 GB of HDD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the instance is optimized for storage capacity rather than raw computational speed or memory throughput. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng fall into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, memory bandwidth for small and large block read operations is weak, though large block write operations achieve average performance. Single-threaded compression and decompression benchmarks, such as gzip and bzip3, register in the bottom 10%, reflecting the legacy architecture of the underlying Intel Xeon processor. Passmark CPU scores are average, but database operations and Redis SET benchmarks remain in the lower 25% performance bracket.

The primary trade-off of the ecs.d1.2xlarge is its massive storage density contrasted with its modest processing capabilities. The inclusion of over 23 TB of local HDD storage makes this instance highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring large-scale sequential data storage where high-speed SSD IOPS are not required. It is well-suited for distributed file systems like Hadoop HDFS, cold data archiving, large-scale log storage, and data warehousing. It is not recommended for high-performance computing, low-latency database transactions, or intensive web serving due to its weak CPU and memory benchmark profiles.
